docs.title: Scopes reference
docs.text:
A complete catalog of every scope string a plugin can declare in manifest.scopes, what each grants, and which ctx member it unlocks. A ctx member is absent unless its scope was granted. Declare least privilege: pick the narrowest verbs your plugin actually needs.

For how grants are enforced at runtime (the Web Worker sandbox, the egress allowlist, secret handling), see security.

The scopes block has exactly six keys, all optional:

"scopes": {
  "graph":     ["node:read", "edge:create"],               // fine-grained graph verbs
  "network":   [ { "endpoint": "https://...", "methods": ["POST"] } ],
  "network_configurable": [ { "config_key": "misp_url", "methods": ["POST"] } ],  // address set by the analyst
  "web_probe": { "purpose": "check whether a profile page exists" },  // desktop only
  "services":  ["rdap"],                                   // Vineyard-operated services, by name
  "config":    [ { "key": "max_concurrency", "type": "number" } ]
}

docs.title: graph
docs.text:
Fine-grained verbs over nodes and edges (node:* / edge:* × read/create/update/delete). A plugin that deletes must declare node:delete / edge:delete explicitly. ctx.graph is present iff at least one graph verb is granted; each method below is present iff its specific verb is granted. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — GraphScope, HostContext.graph.)

Scope string Grants ctx member(s) node:read Read individual nodes, list nodes (optionally by type) ctx.graph.get, ctx.graph.list node:create Create nodes from EntityDrafts ctx.graph.createNode node:update Patch a node's data ctx.graph.updateNode node:delete Delete one node or many in a single bounded op ctx.graph.deleteNode, ctx.graph.deleteNodes edge:read Read all edges; 1-hop neighborhood of a node ctx.graph.edges, ctx.graph.neighbors edge:create Create edges; amend an existing edge (label/data) by its id ctx.graph.createEdge, ctx.graph.updateEdge edge:update Accepted by the schema (backs no method — updateEdge is granted by edge:create) edge:delete Delete one edge or many in a single bounded op ctx.graph.deleteEdge, ctx.graph.deleteEdges

A write verb is not a write

Granting node:create (or any create/update/delete verb) does not let a plugin change the project. Writes are captured into the run's change set and reach the graph only when the analyst reviews that change set and applies it, under their own account.

Bulk ops are one operation

deleteNodes(ids[]) and deleteEdges(ids[]) are a single bounded call, not N separate writes: a legitimate mass-delete (Russian Roulette, Thanos Snap) is issued once, and each id becomes its own item in the run's change set for review. An unknown id fails the whole call.

docs.title: network
docs.text:
Each entry is a NetworkScope object, not a bare string. ctx.net.fetch is present iff at least one network scope is declared. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — NetworkScope, HostContext.net.)

"network": [
  { "endpoint": "https://api.example.com/v1/lookup",
    "methods": ["POST"],
    "purpose": "shown at install" }
]
Field Type Meaning endpoint string Exact origin/path prefix the plugin may reach methods HttpMethod[] Allowed verbs: GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE. An empty list allows every verb purpose string (optional) Human-readable reason, shown at install time

ctx.net.fetch is limited to these endpoints and to the addresses the analyst sets for network_configurable. A URL is matched on its parsed origin (protocol, host and port) plus a path-segment boundary, never as a string prefix — https://h/v1 covers /v1/search but not /v1beta — and on the declared methods. Each request also has its own deadline, response body included: 60 s unless the request's init.timeoutMs sets another (clamped to 1 s – 10 min). A missed deadline rejects with an Error named TimeoutError; see net in the SDK.

The host bridge is the only way out

Plugin code has no network of its own: any fetch, XHR, WebSocket or nested worker the plugin opens itself is refused, on the web and in the desktop app. Use ctx.net.fetch (checked against these endpoints), ctx.net.probe or ctx.service. A dev server does not enforce this, so a pack that calls fetch directly works in development and fails in production. A sandbox-js plugin may declare several endpoints. Cookies are not sent; your request headers pass through as written, including Authorization (see Sending a credential). On desktop, declared endpoints are reachable even without CORS headers, except those on localhost or a loopback or private-network IP address, or on a name that resolves to one, which still need them. A URL on the origin of the Vineyard backend the app is connected to is refused whatever the manifest declares (see Sandbox & security).

docs.title: network_configurable
docs.text:
For a server only the analyst knows the address of: a self-hosted MISP or OpenCTI, or an organisation's own threat-intelligence platform. Each entry names a config key instead of an endpoint, and the address the analyst enters for that key becomes an endpoint of ctx.net.fetch. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — ConfigurableNetworkScope.)

"network_configurable": [
  { "config_key": "misp_url",
    "methods": ["POST"],
    "purpose": "search events on your MISP" }
],
"config": [
  { "key": "misp_url", "label": "MISP URL", "type": "url" },
  { "key": "misp_key", "label": "MISP API key", "type": "string", "secret": true }
]
Field Type Meaning config_key string A scopes.config key of type: "url" in the same plugin. Its value is the endpoint methods HttpMethod[] Allowed verbs, as for network. An empty list allows every verb purpose string (optional) Human-readable reason, shown at install time schemes ("https" | "http")[] (optional) Schemes the address may use. ["https"] when omitted

The address must be a scheme the entry allows, a host and an optional path, such as https://misp.example.org or https://tip.example.org/opencti. One with a user name or password, a ? query or a # fragment is not used. Once set, the address is matched exactly as a network endpoint is: parsed origin, path-segment boundary, methods, and the Vineyard backend's origin refused. Until it is set, or while it is not usable, the entry grants nothing, and ctx.net.fetch rejects with an error that names the setting. The plugin cannot set or change the address: only the analyst can, in the plugin's settings. The Vineyard backend's own address is never usable, and the settings field says so.

An http address works in the desktop app. The web app is served over https, and the browser blocks its requests to an http address as mixed content, so there an http address is not used, and the settings field says so, unless it is on this computer (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]).

An entry whose config_key is not a url setting of the same plugin grants nothing, and registry CI refuses it. CI also refuses methods other than the five upper-case verbs, and any field but the four above: the app matches methods exactly, so "post" would have every request refused.

The install screen shows Network requests to the address you enter in "MISP URL" (https only), followed by the purposes and, when this pack already has an address on this device, the host it is set to. The settings field shows the host requests will go to, or why the address is not used. On the catalog card the scope counts as network.

Your own network

In the desktop app, an address you configure gets the same CORS waiver as a declared endpoint, and the same limit: it stops at the analyst's own network. For a server on this computer or on your organisation's network, such as a MISP on 10.0.0.0/8, the settings field offers Trust … on this computer…, which adds the origin to Additional trusted origins in Desktop Settings after a confirmation dialog. That list applies in every project until you remove the origin there. In the browser, the server must answer CORS for the app's origin itself.

Like network, this scope never attaches a Vineyard credential. Send your server's API key yourself, from a secret setting, as in Sending a credential.

docs.title: web_probe
docs.text:
A single object, not an array. It grants ctx.net.probe — one anonymous request against an arbitrary public host, for plugins such as account discovery that cannot list their endpoints in advance. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — WebProbeScope, HostContext.net.probe.)

"web_probe": { "purpose": "check whether a username has a profile page" }
Field Type Meaning purpose string (optional) Human-readable reason

The host, not the plugin, sets the terms: no cookies and no credentials (Cookie / Authorization / Host are dropped), private and loopback targets refused, and maxBytes / timeoutMs clamped to a ceiling. Redirects are not followed — the caller sees the true status of the URL it asked for, which is what presence detection depends on (a 302 to a login page means "no account"), with the Location returned as redirectUrl.

Desktop only

In the web build ctx.net.probe is absent even when granted. Check for it before calling and fall back (the WhatsMyName pack does exactly this).

docs.title: services
docs.text:
Vineyard-operated services this plugin calls by name. Backs ctx.service, which takes a service name and a path; the base URL is fixed by the app.

"services": ["rdap"]
Name What it is rdap Cached IP RDAP lookups, normalized across every RIR telegram Read-only Telegram reconnaissance, on an account Vineyard operates

A closed enum, so a typo fails at review. A service scope is not covered by scopes_summary.network on the catalog card; it appears as its own services field.

const res = await ctx.service('rdap', '8.8.8.8');
const who = await ctx.service('telegram', 'resolve', {
    method: 'POST',
    body: JSON.stringify({ target: 'durov' }),
});

Authorization on a service call is ignored — the host sets it. init.timeoutMs and the request deadline work as for ctx.net.fetch. Some services are restricted to named packs; telegram is one.

A service call needs a Vineyard account. In local mode the Marketplace does not install a pack that declares services (its Install button is disabled, with the tooltip "Needs a Vineyard account — sign in to use this pack"), and in a pack installed earlier ctx.service throws service '<name>' needs a Vineyard account.

docs.title: config
docs.text:
Each entry is a ConfigValue. ctx.config is a read-only map of the declared keys the analyst has set a value for, secret ones included, coerced to the declared type. It is absent while none of them has a value, so read it as ctx.config?.key ?? DEFAULT. Values are kept per signed-in account — in the OS keychain on desktop (only until the app quits on a computer that cannot encrypt them), for the tab session in the browser. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — ConfigValue, HostContext.config.)

Members of the same Plugin Pack that declare a key and call the same set of network origins share one value for it, so the analyst enters it once. The origins are the scheme, host and port of the member's scopes.network endpoints; paths do not matter, so members calling different paths on one API host share. Each network_configurable entry counts as one more destination, named by its config_key, so members that read the same address setting and call the same fixed hosts share both the address and the key that goes to it. A plugin published on its own, or one with no scopes.network or network_configurable entry, keeps its own values, and two packs never share a value even when they call the same host. A member that calls one more origin than the others keeps its own value, so give members that should share a key the same origins. Sharing does not widen what a plugin receives: each plugin still gets only the keys its own manifest declares.

Field Type Meaning key string Identifier, pattern ^[a-z0-9_]+$ label string (optional) Field label in the plugin's Settings section of the Run plugins dialog and in Settings → Keys & Secrets type "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "url" | "enum" Value type enum string[] (optional) Allowed values when type is enum secret boolean (optional) BYOK-style credential; see below scope "plugin" | "project" | "user" (optional) Where the value is stored. Accepted but not read; values are stored and shared as described above optional boolean (optional) If false/absent the field is marked "required by this plugin" (not enforced; the plugin must handle a missing value)

secret semantics

secret: true does not hide the value from the plugin. The value IS delivered to the declaring plugin as ctx.config[key], since the plugin is what calls the API with it. The flag masks the form field. The value is never recorded in a task record or an AI conversation, because credentials are kept out of params. See security.

docs.title: Not scopes
docs.text:
The following are always available and grant no authority over data or network. They require no declaration. (Source: the SDK's sdk.ts types — HostContext.)

Capability ctx member Notes params ctx.params This run's user input (read-only). Not validated against the params JSON Schema: the Run dialog only checks that required fields are filled, so validate types yourself progress ctx.progress.set Drives the task row: percent sets its progress and message is shown after the plugin's name. phase is accepted but not shown log ctx.progress.log Accepted but currently a no-op; nothing is recorded status ctx.progress.status Accepted but currently a no-op; the task state is set by the runner signal ctx.signal, ctx.onCancel Cooperative cancel — the plugin MUST observe it

Two members are also always present and not gated: ctx.run (this run's identity — runId, projectId, pluginId, grantedScopes, platform) and ctx.input (the trigger context, including selection).

A scope-0 plugin

The Chaos pack's Dumb AI Optimizer declares no scopes at all. It still gets ctx.params, ctx.progress, and ctx.signal — but ctx.graph, ctx.net, and ctx.config are all undefined.

docs.title: Type Pack schema
docs.text:
Exhaustive field reference for typepack.schema.json — the authoring contract for a vineyard:typepack document. Neither registry CI nor the app validates a document against it; run it in your own CI, as the reference pack repos do. A Type Pack declares the node entity types that extend the graph's vocabulary. For a conceptual walkthrough and authoring guidance, see Developing Type Packs.

Canonical schema

$id: https://vineyard.run/schemas/typepack.json · JSON Schema draft 2020-12. The document is the source of truth; this page enumerates it field-by-field.

docs.title: Top-level object
docs.text:
The root is an object with additionalProperties: false — unknown keys fail schema validation.

Required: identifier, name, content_type, version, summary, description, types.

Field Type Req Constraints / default Meaning identifier string yes pattern ^(?:[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\.){2,}typepacks\.[a-z0-9]+(?:[._-][a-z0-9]+)*$ Reverse-DNS id, e.g. run.vineyard.typepacks.infrastructure. content_type string yes const: "vineyard:typepack" Discriminator marking the document as a Type Pack. name string yes minLength: 1, maxLength: 128 Human-readable pack name. version string yes SemVer pattern ^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$ SemVer of the pack content. MAJOR = breaking type change; nodes that use the changed type may need updating. summary string yes 1–250 chars, one line The line under the pack's name. See A pack's line and its page. description string yes 1–16,000 chars The pack's page, in Markdown. A document without summary predates the page and has this as its one line; the app still reads one, the registry lists none. authors array<object> no see Authors Attribution list. license string no — SPDX expression, e.g. MIT, Apache-2.0, CC-BY-4.0. marketing_url string no format: uri Landing page for the pack. thumbnail_url string no format: uri Icon/thumbnail image. types array<entityType> yes minItems: 1 Node entity type definitions.

docs.title: identifierSegment
docs.text:
Several keys (category, name, property keys) reuse the identifierSegment definition:

Rule Value type string pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ (snake_case, must start with a lowercase letter) maxLength 31

docs.title: Authors
docs.text:
authors[] — array of objects, each additionalProperties: false.

Field Type Req Constraints name string yes — email string no format: email url string no format: uri

docs.title: Entity type (types[])
docs.text:
Each item in types defines one node entity type (#/$defs/entityType, additionalProperties: false). Required: category, name, label_property, properties.

Field Type Req Constraints / default Meaning category identifierSegment yes snake_case, ≤31 Grouping namespace, e.g. infrastructure. name identifierSegment yes snake_case, ≤31 Type name within the category, e.g. ip_address. display_name string no — Human label for the type. description string no — What the type represents. label_property string yes must name a key in properties that is non-optional The property key used as the node's display label. icon string no polymorphic (see below) Node icon. When absent, the node renders with color only. color string no pattern ^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$ Node color #rrggbb. When absent, a stable color is derived from category.name. properties object yes minProperties: 1; keys are identifierSegment; values are property property key → property schema. Must be non-empty. identity_properties array<string> no minItems: 1, uniqueItems; each item MUST name a key in properties Keys that together identify one entity, for de-duplication. Defaults to [label_property]. E.g. identity.account has username as its label_property but is identified by (username, platform). label_template string no referenced keys MUST exist in properties Display label built from several properties, e.g. "{username} · {platform}". Falls back to label_property when any referenced field is empty, so a partially-filled node never shows a dangling separator. Display only — de-duplication uses identity_properties.

The fully qualified type reference is category.name (e.g. infrastructure.ip_address). That qualified form is what Node.type stores and what reference targets point at.

Icon resolution order

icon is polymorphic and resolved in order: a data: / http(s): image URI; else a kebab-case lucide icon name (e.g. shield-alert); else a literal glyph/emoji. Any kebab-case lucide name resolves.

docs.title: Property object
docs.text:
The schema for each value in a properties map (#/$defs/property, additionalProperties: false). Required: type — every property must declare an explicit type.

Field Type Req Constraints / default Meaning type string (enum) yes see type enum Logical property type. description string no — Human description of the property. optional boolean no default: false false ⇒ required key in Node.data. Write it on every property: creating a node refuses a missing key only when the property says "optional": false explicitly. With optional left out, the Properties panel marks the property required (*), but a create without it is accepted. case_insensitive boolean no default: false Fold case when this property is part of the de-duplication identity; display and storage keep what was written. Right for handles, domains, hostnames, emails and hex digests; wrong for Base58 crypto addresses, URL paths and case-sensitive file paths. A crypto address property mixes Base58 with hex and bech32, where case means nothing; give it normalize instead. Beside normalize: hostname, ip or cidr, set it too: an app that does not know the rule then still folds case. A missing flag produces a visible, mergeable duplicate, while a wrong one silently merges two entities. normalize string (enum) no crypto_address, hex, hostname, ip, cidr or url; case_insensitive: true only beside hostname, ip and cidr A named rule for the de-duplication identity, for what case_insensitive cannot describe. Display and storage keep what was written. hostname folds a DNS name: one trailing dot dropped, an internationalised name to punycode (IDNA, UTS #46), lower case. The mapping never reads a name as an IPv4 address: a non-ASCII name folds as the ASCII name it maps to, so a full-width ０ｘ７ｆ.１ folds as 0x7f.1, not as 127.0.0.1. ip folds an IPv6 address to its RFC 5952 form (lower case, no leading zeros, the longest zero run as ::; an IPv4-mapped address keeps its dotted tail and is not folded into that IPv4 address) and an IPv4 address padded to three digits per part (192.000.002.001) to its plain form, but only when every part that starts with a zero is 000 to 007, which read the same in octal and decimal. An address with any other leading zero is compared as written, a padded part such as the 010 of 010.001.002.003 included, because browsers and inet_aton read 010 as octal 8. cidr folds the address as ip does and the prefix length, without clearing host bits. url folds an http, https, ftp, ws or wss URL as a browser parses it — scheme and host in lower case, the host in punycode without a trailing dot, no default port, . and .. resolved, an empty path as / — with percent-encoding in one form (RFC 3986 §6.2.2); its path, query and fragment keep their case. crypto_address and hex decide per value, for a property whose values mix formats where case matters with formats where it does not: crypto_address folds by the value's format: 0x + 40 hex (EIP-55 case is a checksum), bech32/bech32m with a known prefix (bc, tb, bcrt, ltc, tltc, btg, bnb, addr, addr_test, stake, stake_test) and a valid checksum, and TON raw <workchain>:<64 hex> go to lower case; a CashAddr, with or without bitcoincash:, goes to its lower-case payload; anything else, Base58 included, is compared exactly as written. hex folds a 64-hex value, with or without 0x, to lower case without the 0x. Neither re-encodes, so a value that only matches after conversion (a TRON hex address, a Litecoin 3… alias, a TON user-friendly address) must be written in its canonical form. An app that does not know the rule falls back to case_insensitive. The agent's common_ground and aggregate_values compare values by this rule too, by property name across every installed type: a property of that name on any type follows it, losing the case and spacing folding it would otherwise get, and a name two packs give different rules is compared exactly as written. Declare it only on a property name that means the same thing in every pack that uses it. duplicate_key boolean no default: false; a scalar property outside the identity Marks a canonical form of the identity filled after the node was made, such as a phone number's e164 beside the number as written. Nodes of the type with the same value here are reported as duplicates of each other (see Duplicates and merging), although their identities differ. Not part of the identity: filling it never merges nodes by itself. Compared with the property's own case_insensitive or normalize. default any no should match type (not checked) Accepted but not applied: nothing in the app fills an absent key from it. validator object no see validator Structured validation rules. enum array conditional minItems: 1; items string|number|boolean Required when type = "enum". reference object conditional see reference Required when type = "reference".

docs.title: Property type enum
docs.text:
type must be one of:

string, text, number, integer, boolean, date, datetime, enum, url, ip, hash, email, reference, array, object

Value Notes string Single-line string. text Multi-line / long text. number Floating-point number. integer Whole number. boolean true/false. date Calendar date. datetime Timestamp. enum Constrained set — see enum array. url URL string. ip IP address (IPv4/IPv6). hash Hash digest. email Email address. reference Link to another node type — see reference object. array List value. object Nested object value.

No secret/credential types

The enum deliberately omits secret and credential. Do not model API keys, tokens, or passwords as node/edge properties.

docs.title: validator object
docs.text:
additionalProperties: false. Structured validation. All fields are optional; combine as needed.

Field Type Constraints Meaning regex string — ECMAScript regex tested against a string value as written, with no implicit anchoring: write ^…$ to require a full match. Skipped for values over 4,096 characters, for a pattern that does not compile, and for a pattern with a backtracking-prone shape. min number — Minimum numeric value. max number — Maximum numeric value. min_length integer minimum: 0 Minimum string length. A hint; the app does not check it. max_length integer minimum: 0 Maximum string length. A hint; the app does not check it. format string — Named format hint, e.g. ipv4, sha256, iso8601. The app does not check it.

docs.title: reference object
docs.text:
Required when type = "reference". additionalProperties: false.

Field Type Meaning target string Qualified category.name of the referenced node type, or * for any.

docs.title: Annotated example: Infrastructure Type Pack
docs.text:
A trimmed, fully valid vineyard:typepack showing the top-level block, two node types (covering ip, enum, string and integer property types plus validator variants). Comments are annotations only — JSON does not permit them.

{
  "identifier": "run.vineyard.typepacks.infrastructure", // reverse-DNS id
  "content_type": "vineyard:typepack",                 // discriminator (const)
  "version": "1.0.0",                                  // pack CONTENT SemVer
  "name": "VINEYARD Type Pack - Infrastructure",
  "description": "Network infrastructure CTI entities.",
  "authors": [{ "name": "VINEYARD", "url": "https://vineyard.run" }],
  "license": "Apache-2.0",                             // SPDX expression
  "marketing_url": "https://vineyard.run/typepacks/infrastructure",
  "thumbnail_url": "https://vineyard.run/typepacks/infrastructure/icon.png",

  "types": [
    {
      "category": "infrastructure",                    // qualified type => infrastructure.ip_address
      "name": "ip_address",
      "display_name": "IP Address",
      "description": "An IPv4 or IPv6 network address.",
      "label_property": "ip_address",                  // MUST be a non-optional property below
      "icon": "network",                               // lucide icon name
      "color": "#60a5fa",                              // #rrggbb
      "properties": {
        "ip_address": {
          "type": "ip",
          "description": "The IP address.",
          "optional": false,                           // => required key in Node.data
          "validator": { "format": "ip" }              // named format hint
        },
        "version": {
          "type": "enum",
          "optional": true,
          "enum": ["ipv4", "ipv6"]                     // required for type=enum
        },
        "country_code": {
          "type": "string",
          "optional": true,
          "validator": { "regex": "^[A-Z]{2}$" }       // anchored: the whole value must match
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "category": "infrastructure",
      "name": "autonomous_system",
      "display_name": "Autonomous System",
      "label_property": "autonomous_system_number",
      "icon": "waypoints",
      "color": "#818cf8",
      "properties": {
        "autonomous_system_number": {
          "type": "integer",
          "optional": false,
          "validator": { "min": 0, "max": 4294967295 } // numeric bounds
        },
        "autonomous_system_name": { "type": "string", "optional": true }
      }
    }
  ]
}

More patterns in the real pack

The shipped Infrastructure pack also shows that category does not have to match within one pack (it defines both infrastructure.* and web.* types), and the hash/date/datetime/text types (in whois_record and certificate). See the Type Packs guide.

docs.title: Validation notes
docs.text:
• Every top-level, entity, property, and nested block sets additionalProperties: false — unknown keys fail validation.
  • label_property must name a key that exists in properties and is non-optional.
  • enum is required precisely when type = "enum"; reference is required precisely when type = "reference".
  • The last two are authoring rules. The schema states them only in descriptions, so even a schema validator does not enforce them, and nothing else does.
  • A property with normalize: crypto_address, hex or url cannot also set "case_insensitive": true; the schema rejects the pair, because the flag would fold what those rules keep.
  • Registry CI checks a Type Pack document only for this: its identifier, content_type and version match the entry; type_count, and icon when the entry carries one, match the document; every identity_properties key names an existing property that is not array, object or json; every normalize is one of the six rules, beside case_insensitive: true only for hostname, ip and cidr, on a property that is not array, object or json; every duplicate_key is a boolean on such a property outside the identity; and no other published Type Pack defines the same category.name (see Publishing).
  • The app checks node data against the declared properties when a node is written; see What the app checks on node data.
  • The registry entry that lists a pack pins it to an immutable commit SHA; registry CI rejects tags and branches (see registry schema).
